claims: The last human moon landing was Apollo 17.
Apollo 17 landed on the Moon on December 11, 1972.
NASA astronauts Eugene Cernan and Harrison Schmitt spent over three days exploring the Taurus-Littrow valley.
Apollo 17 was NASA's final Apollo mission.
Apollo 17 landed in the Taurus-Littrow Valley.
The last people on the Moon were Eugene Cernan (Commander) and Harrison Schmitt (Lunar Module Pilot).
Eugene Cernan was the last to leave the lunar surface on December 14, 1972.
Apollo 17 crew spent approximately 73 hours on the lunar surface.
Apollo 17 crew completed three successful long-duration excursions.
Apollo 17 was the first mission to include a trained scientist.
Apollo 17 collected the most samples of any Apollo mission.
Apollo 17 performed the most experiments of any Apollo mission.
NASA's Apollo program ended with Apollo 17.
